specification.problem: Given a unitary representation of a finite group G on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, find a state whose G-translates are distinguishable with the highest probability. Apply this to quantum oracle problems: GROUP MULTIPLICATION (determine the product of an ordered tuple of group elements by querying elements; for two elements, a single quantum query succeeds with probability 2/|G|, which is optimal and generalizes Deutsch's algorithm from Z_2) and the HIDDEN CONJUGATING ELEMENT PROBLEM (oracle conjugates by an unknown group element; for many groups, e.g. dihedral and symmetric, the element is found with probability 1 using one query).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the problem statements and the success-probability claims; the optimal-state construction, circuits and measurements are not given in the abstract and are left to later parts.

equations.label: Product of two group elements: success probability
equations.description: Optimal single-query success probability for finding the product of two elements of G.
equations.abstract_quote: we give an algorithm to find the product of two elements of $G$ with a single quantum query with probability $2/|G|$
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract; optimality is also claimed.

registers.name: H_rep
registers.role: Register holding the probe state |\psi\rangle, acted on by \rho(g) through the oracle

specification.initial_state: An optimal probe state |\psi\rangle in H maximizing the success probability of distinguishing the translates \rho(g)|\psi\rangle. The abstract does not give its explicit form.

steps.description: Prepare the optimal probe state |\psi\rangle in the representation space H.
Make one oracle query, which applies \rho(g) for the unknown group-dependent element g (for the hidden conjugating element problem, the conjugation action). The state becomes \rho(g)|\psi\rangle.
Distinguish the translates \rho(g)|\psi\rangle. For the product of two elements this succeeds with probability 2/|G|.

specification.measurement: A single discrimination measurement (a POVM on H) is applied to the post-query state \rho(g)|\psi\rangle to identify g (or the product/hidden element). The abstract states only that the optimal state maximizes distinguishability; the explicit POVM is not given. Expected success is 2/|G| for the product of two elements and 1 for the hidden conjugating element on e.g. dihedral and symmetric groups.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map the measurement outcome to a group element label, and for group multiplication to the product of the two elements. No further processing is specified in the abstract.
assumptions: The oracle is modeled as applying a unitary representation \rho(g) of the queried or hidden group element to the probe state; this is a generic assumption, not the paper's explicit construction.
Oracle modeled generically as applying \rho(g) to the probe state.
Measurement is assumed to be an optimal discrimination POVM, whose form is not given in the abstract.
